c.tagline: Where turquoise lagoons meet a laid-back Melanesian capital.

taxi.color: No standard color; identify by plates starting with 'T'
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered - agree on a price with the driver before departing. Short in-town trips typically run 300-800 VT.

emergency.note: Fire: 113. Medical facilities are limited outside central Port Vila; comprehensive travel/medevac insurance is strongly recommended.

avoid.reason: Petty theft and occasional bag-snatching after dark around nightspots and the waterfront — take taxis at night.

hood_desc: The compact harbourfront core packed with the produce and fish market, duty-free shops, restaurants and the main wharf; best for first-timers who want everything walkable and easy access to tours and ferries.
A calm turquoise lagoon a short drive south of downtown lined with resort hotels, some with overwater bungalows; suits couples and families wanting a beach-resort base close to town and the airport.

A private resort island a 3-minute ferry ride across the harbour from downtown, paired with budget and mid-range waterfront guesthouses on the mainland shore; good for travelers wanting an island feel without leaving the city behind.

A breezy southern headland with surf breaks, sunset views and a more local village atmosphere about 15-20 minutes from town; popular with surfers, divers and travelers seeking a quieter, adults-oriented stay.

West of town near Mele village and the Mele Cascades waterfall, home to the marine-sanctuary islet of Hideaway Island; suited to snorkelers, divers and those wanting a laid-back beach base outside the capital.

water.note: Town water supply is treated and generally safe, though high mineral content can upset sensitive stomachs.

transit.pay: Pay the driver directly in cash (vatu) when boarding or leaving a minibus - there is no ticket, farecard, or app system. Taxi and resort-boat fares are also cash, agreed or confirmed before the trip.
transit.hours: Minibuses run roughly 6am-11pm with no fixed timetable or stops; hail one from the roadside. There is no public transport after dark - taxis (bookable through hotels) are the after-hours option.
transit.note: There are no numbered routes or stops - flag down any shared minibus (plates starting with 'B') heading your way and tell the driver where you're going.

bus: Shared minibuses around Port Vila and Efate (no fixed routes)
Efate island buses/minivans to Mele, Pango, Eratap and Havannah Harbour

transit.m: Taxi (unmetered, ~15 min, fare agreed in advance)

tip.r: Tipping is not part of local custom and is not expected at restaurants, hotels, or for taxis/drivers; resorts occasionally add a service charge instead.

food.name: Lap lap
food.desc: Vanuatu's national dish: grated yam, taro or banana pounded to a paste, soaked in coconut cream, wrapped in banana leaf and baked in a stone oven.

places.name: Port Vila Market House
places.note: Mamas cook it to old family recipes; the most authentic lap lap in town, cheap and filling.

places.name: Waterfront food trucks
places.note: Evening vans serving lap lap, grilled fish and rice plates cooked in front of you.

places.name: Wan Smolbag Nutrition Centre Cafe
places.note: Community-run kitchen doing traditional island food with local produce.

food.name: Tuluk
food.desc: A grated-cassava parcel wrapped around minced pork or beef, bound in banana leaf and baked. Vanuatu's answer to a hot savoury pastry, eaten with the hands.

places.name: Port Vila Market House
places.note: Sold warm from covered trays; ask the mamas which parcel is freshest.

places.name: Waterfront food trucks
places.note: Late-afternoon staple alongside lap lap; a few hundred vatu each.

places.name: Fresh Wota roadside stalls
places.note: Neighbourhood stalls where locals buy tuluk on the way home from work.

food.name: Coconut crab
food.desc: Vanuatu's legendary land crab, sweet and nutty from a diet of coconut, usually grilled with garlic butter. Now tightly managed, so supply is limited.

places.name: L'Houstalet
places.note: Long-standing French-Ni-Vanuatu restaurant known for island specialities; call ahead to check availability.

places.name: Tamanu on the Beach
places.note: Beachfront kitchen that features it when it is legally in season and sourced locally.

places.name: The Beach Bar
places.note: Sunset spot with seafood grills; a good fallback if crab is off the menu.

food.name: Grilled poulet fish
food.desc: Firm white reef fish, split and grilled over coals with lime and coconut, served with island cabbage and rice. Landed the same morning off Efate.

places.name: Port Vila Market House
places.note: Fish counter plus hot stalls that grill the catch with rice for a few hundred vatu.

places.name: Nambawan Cafe
places.note: Harbour-front cafe with a reliable grilled fish of the day and seawall views.

places.name: The Beach Bar
places.note: Casual beachfront grill doing island fish plates and fish burgers at sunset.

food.name: Santo grass-fed beef
food.desc: Vanuatu's organic, grass-fed cattle from Espiritu Santo produce excellent steaks, exported across the Pacific and grilled simply on the waterfront.

places.name: Waterfront Bar and Grill
places.note: Harbour-side grill where the local sirloin and rib fillet are the reason to go.

places.name: L'Houstalet
places.note: French treatment of local beef; an old-school Port Vila dining room.

places.name: Tamanu on the Beach
places.note: Smart beachfront restaurant pairing Santo beef with island vegetables.

food.name: Raw fish in coconut milk
food.desc: Tuna or reef fish cured in lime then folded through fresh coconut milk with onion, tomato and chilli. Served cold, and impossible to eat just one bowl of.

places.name: Nambawan Cafe
places.note: Easy harbour-front spot for a cold bowl with a Tusker in the shade.

places.name: The Beach Bar
places.note: Beach seating and a short menu of island seafood done well.

places.name: Port Vila Market House
places.note: Market kitchens make it fresh daily at a fraction of restaurant prices.

food.name: Kava
food.desc: Vanuatu's signature drink, pressed from fresh kava root and drunk in a single shell. Nakamals open at dusk and drinking kava is a nightly ritual, not a novelty.

places.name: Ronnie's Nakamal
places.note: Well-known visitor-friendly nakamal; look for the red lamp that means kava is being served.

places.name: Tagabe nakamals
places.note: Strip of neighbourhood nakamals with the strongest local brews; go early evening and keep voices low.

places.name: Nambatri nakamals
places.note: Small local shells-and-stools setups; buy a shell, drink it in one, then sit quietly.

food.name: Tusker lager
food.desc: Vanuatu's own beer, brewed in Port Vila and drunk ice cold on every waterfront terrace. The standard chaser after a shell of kava.

places.name: Waterfront Bar and Grill
places.note: Yacht-club atmosphere and the classic sundowner spot in town.

places.name: Nambawan Cafe
places.note: Harbour views, all-day opening and cold Tusker on tap.

places.name: The Beach Bar
places.note: Toes-in-the-sand drinking with a fire pit after dark.

landmarks: Iririki Island Resort
A lush little island resort just offshore from downtown, reachable by a quick ferry hop, with sweeping harbor views that make it one of the most photographed vistas in the capital.
Port Vila Harbour Waterfront
Stroll the palm-lined promenade along one of the South Pacific's most beautiful natural harbors, dotted with cafes, markets, and views of moored yachts against a turquoise backdrop.
Port Vila Central Market
A vibrant, colorful hub where ni-Vanuatu vendors sell tropical produce, kava, and handicrafts — the beating heart of local life and a feast for the senses.
Mele Cascades
A short drive from the city, these tiered turquoise waterfalls tumble through rainforest into natural swimming pools, one of the island's most iconic natural landmarks.
Chief Roi Mata's Domain (UNESCO Site)
Vanuatu's only UNESCO World Heritage Site, comprising sacred sites linked to a legendary 17th-century paramount chief — a powerful glimpse into ni-Vanuatu history and spirituality.
Ekasup Cultural Village
An immersive traditional village experience near town where guides demonstrate ancient hunting, medicine, and customs of the Ekasup community.
National Museum of Vanuatu
Compact but fascinating, this museum showcases sand drawings, tribal artifacts, and the layered history of the archipelago's many islands and cultures.
Parliament House of Vanuatu
Distinctive for its bold, colorful nakamal-inspired architecture, this government building is a striking symbol of the young nation's independence and identity.
Rentapao (Teouma) Blue Hole
A stunning natural swimming hole of impossibly blue freshwater fringed by jungle, popular for rope swings and a refreshing escape from the tropical heat.
Hideaway Island Marine Sanctuary
A tiny protected island just off Efate famed for its underwater post office and vibrant coral reef, perfect for snorkeling and photography above and below the waves.

train.note: Vanuatu has no railway (only a tiny colonial-era line once existed on Efate). Travel around Efate is by minibus, taxi or rental car, and between islands by ferry or Air Vanuatu domestic flights.

bus.note: No international coaches - Vanuatu is an island group. In Port Vila, red-plate 'B' minibuses act as a shared hop-on service: flag one down, tell the driver your destination and pay a flat town fare. There is no scheduled intercity bus network.

ferry.note: No international passenger ferries. Domestically, the 'Big Sista' passenger ferry (Vanuatu Ferry Ltd) links Port Vila with Lakatoro (Malekula) and Luganville (Espiritu Santo), and cargo/passenger boats such as Vanuatu Cargo serve other islands. Sailings are weather-dependent and can be cancelled in rough seas; book at the operator's Port Vila office by the seafront.

half.name: Eton Beach
half.blurb: Sandy beach on Efate's east coast, about 45 minutes from town, sits beside a freshwater lagoon good for swimming.

half.name: Havannah Harbour
half.blurb: Sheltered bay on Efate's northwest coast, about an hour's drive, was a US naval base during World War II and now draws divers to its wrecks.

full.name: Mount Yasur
full.blurb: Active volcano on Tanna Island, reached by a short flight, lets visitors stand near a crater rim glowing with lava at night.
